title: Silca Ressurects Omata: the Iconic Analog Cycling Computer
content:
Silca just announced it acquired and resurrected Omata, the world’s first analog cycling computer with internal GPS. After the announcement, Silca will release a limited run of the iconic Omata ($800) devices, made in-house at its Indianapolis facility…

Silca Omata Quick Hits

  • Made in-house at Silca
  • $800
  • Distraction-Free Analog Dial: Clean mechanical interface displaying speed, distance, ascent, and ride time.
  • Digital in the Background: GPS internal computer records standard FIT files for training logs and data transfer.
  • Improved Weather Resistance: Triple-barrier lip seal around bezel and Gore-Tex membrane over the barometric pressure sensor.
  • Seamless Syncing: Quick .fit file uploads via the Omata Utility App for iOS or via a USB-C connection.
  • Smart Tracking: Features Auto-Pause and GPS-Fix to seamlessly track your route without manual intervention.
  • Omata is iOS-compatible only.
  • New Mounting System: Omata works with existing Garmin or Wahoo mounts.

Omata Refresh

Longtime readers of The Radavist will remember when Omata first launched back in 2016. At the time, it was the world’s first mechatronic cycling computer (a digital unit with analog movement), and it presents a refined yet restrained design without sacrificing the performance expected of a modern digital device. Built as an intentional alternative to screen-fatiguing, noisy digital electronics, Omata captures data silently in the background while displaying real-time metrics through a mechanical dial.

Made by Silca

Encased in an aluminum housing, Omata features an intuitive rotating bezel for switching modes, USB-C charging, improved weather resistance, and integrated ANT+ connectivity. With its latest firmware update, available to Apple iOS users, Omata can seamlessly pair with external sensors to record ride analytics such as power and heart rate, keeping the interface distraction-free while capturing essential information in the background.

Silca redesigned Omata’s internal circuit board, battery system, and outer housing around the legacy analog “movements” to modernize the hardware. Production and final assembly were moved to the brand’s Indianapolis facility, making it one of the only cycling computers assembled in the United States. The Silca team also redesigned the instrument’s weather sealing, integrating a custom triple-barrier lip seal for the rotating bezel and a Gore-Tex membrane over the barometric pressure sensor for improved moisture resistance, while also adding a versatile square mounting cleat compatible with standard Garmin or Wahoo mounts, allowing riders to swap between computers and bikes easily.

Release and Production

Because Silca’s production run is limited and production is not quick, Silca will be releasing Omata in small batches until sold out. This limited production model does make these units only available in the US. Please reach to Silca out if you are international and interested in a unit.
